newsitem.title: RUSSIA: Russian grain buying for reserves lags 1995 level.
newsitem.headline: Russian grain buying for reserves lags 1995 level.

text.p: The Russian government's purchases of grain from domestic producers are lagging behind 1995 levels, an Agriculture Ministry official said on Friday.

In comments carried by Interfax news agency, Ivan Gridasov, head of the ministry's crop-growing department, said state reserves of all kinds had 7.49 million tonnes of grain, including 4.21 million tonnes of food wheat, as of mid-October.
Total wheat purchases were lagging by 571,000 tonnes, and buying of other grains by 339,000 tonnes, on year-ago levels.
Gridasov said that the pace of purchases by the Federal Food Corporation, which secures supplies for big cities and the armed forces, was alarmingly low.
The fund had bought only 355,000 tonnes of grain as of mid-October out of a targeted 4.5 million tonnes.
Regional reserves in the Stavropol grain belt stood at only 106,000 tonnes.

Gridasov blamed the low prices offered by the state for the slow filling of reserves. Stavropol farmers were offered 709,000 roubles per tonne of wheat and Rostov producers were offered 533,000 roubles per tonne.
He said the state had concluded contracts for 8.3 million tonnes of grain, including 472,000 tonnes for the Federal Food Corporation. --Moscow Newsroom +7095 941 8520 ($1 = 5,434 roubles)
